mainTopic: The opening משנה of מסכת סוטה on קינוי and witnesses, why סוטה follows נזיר, an אגדה on matching couples, and why one witness is believed about טומאה
overview: The משנה opens with a מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. Both agree that the warning (קינוי) needs two witnesses, but they disagree about how many witnesses are needed for the seclusion (סתירה). If she only speaks with the man, nothing changes. If she is secluded with him long enough for intimacy, she becomes forbidden to her husband and to תרומה, and she does חליצה rather than יבום. The גמרא first explains why סוטה follows נזיר: it follows רבי's lesson that anyone who sees a סוטה in her disgrace should keep away from wine, and a chain of topics from כתובות to נדרים to נזיר explains why נזיר comes first. It then reads ״הַמְקַנֵּא״ to mean that a husband should not warn in the first place. Next comes an אגדה from ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן about how couples are matched, which the גמרא settles by splitting first and second marriages. Finally, the גמרא shows that both תנאים agree one witness is believed about actual טומאה. It begins proving this from the פסוק ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How many witnesses for the warning and for the drinking
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree the warning needs two witnesses. They argue over how many witnesses are needed for the seclusion that brings her to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: A husband who warns his wife: רבי אליעזר says he warns her in front of two witnesses, and he can make her drink based on one witness, or even based on what he himself saw. רבי יהושע says he warns her in front of two, and he can make her drink only based on two.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the מסכת with a מחלוקת about how many witnesses are needed at two stages: the warning, and the seclusion that leads to the bitter water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that the warning (קינוי) needs two witnesses. The argument is only about the seclusion (סתירה). רבי אליעזר holds one witness, or even the husband himself, is enough, while רבי יהושע demands full testimony of two.

keyTerms.meaning: One who warns (his wife not to be alone with a certain man)
The husband's formal warning
Based on two witnesses
He has her drink (the bitter water)
A single witness

steps.confusionAlert: The two תנאים do NOT argue about the warning. Both say it needs two witnesses. Their whole argument is about the second stage, the seclusion that leads to drinking.

phrases.english: One who warns his wife
Rabbi Eliezer says:
He warns her in front of two witnesses,
and has her drink based on one witness,
phrases.notes: The one witness is testifying that he saw her alone with the man after the warning.

phrases.english: or based on himself.
phrases.notes: The husband himself saw them alone together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
He warns her in front of two witnesses,
and has her drink based on two witnesses.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Warning needs two witnesses according to everyone. For the seclusion, רבי אליעזר accepts one witness or the husband himself, and רבי יהושע requires two.

steps.title: How the warning is given, and why just talking changes nothing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the warning in front of two witnesses and rules that if she only spoke with the man, she stays permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he warn her? He says to her in front of two witnesses: 'Do not speak with so-and-so.' If she then spoke with him, she is still permitted to her husband and still permitted to eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how a valid warning is given, then teaches that simply talking with the man after the warning does not change her status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning is worded as 'do not speak with him,' but breaking that wording by talking alone has no legal effect. She stays permitted to her husband and, if married to a כהן, to תרומה. This prepares for the next line, which says what actually does change her status.

keyTerms.meaning: How?
So-and-so, a specific man
Permitted to her home, meaning to live with her husband
The holy portion given to כהנים, which a כהן's wife may eat

phrases.english: How does he warn her?
He says to her in front of two witnesses:
"Do not speak with so-and-so,"
and she spoke with him:
she is still permitted to her home
phrases.notes: "Her home" is a polite way of saying she may still be with her husband.

phrases.english: and permitted to eat תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the warning mentioned in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A warning is given before two witnesses. Merely speaking with the man afterward does not forbid her.

steps.title: Seclusion after the warning makes her forbidden
steps.stepSummary: If she secluded herself with the man long enough for intimacy, she becomes forbidden to her husband and to תרומה. If the husband dies, she does חליצה and not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she went into a hidden place with him and stayed there long enough to become impure, she is forbidden to her husband and forbidden to eat תרומה. And if her husband dies, she does חליצה and does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the case that does change her status: being secluded with the man for enough time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seclusion (סתירה) after a warning creates a real doubt that she was unfaithful. Because of that doubt she is forbidden to her husband and to תרומה. For the same reason, if he dies without children she cannot do יבום and instead does חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A hidden, private place
Enough time for intimacy
She does חליצה (the release ceremony)
She does יבום (marries the brother-in-law)

steps.whatToRemember: Talking with the man after the warning changes nothing. Seclusion long enough for intimacy makes her forbidden to her husband and to תרומה, and if he dies, she does חליצה and not יבום.

phrases.english: If she went in with him to a hidden place
and stayed with him long enough for impurity:
phrases.notes: "Impurity" here means intimacy, so this is enough time for them to have been together.

phrases.english: she is forbidden to her home,
and forbidden to eat תרומה.
And if he died:
phrases.notes: "He" is the husband, who died without children before she drank.

phrases.english: she does חליצה and does not do יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 2: seclusion, not speech, changes her status
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seclusion long enough for intimacy forbids her to her husband and to תרומה, and requires חליצה rather than יבום.

steps.title: Why does סוטה come right after נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what connects מסכת נזיר to מסכת סוטה, since the order of the משנה puts them next to each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Now, the תנא has just come from מסכת נזיר. What did he teach there that led him to teach סוטה next?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking about the order of the מסכתות: why does סוטה follow נזיר? This sets up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נזיר is about vows of abstinence and seems to have nothing to do with a suspected wife. The גמרא assumes the order of the משנה is deliberate, so it wants to know the link.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and analyzes the משנה
Now, since (opening a question)
Came up from, finished
מסכת נזיר, which comes before סוטה

phrases.english: Gemara
Now, the tanna has come up from נזיר,
what did he teach there
that leads him to teach סוטה?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי תַּנָּא מִנָּזִיר סָלֵיק, מַאי תְּנָא דְּקָא תָּנֵא סוֹטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא with a question about the placement of the whole מסכת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The connection between מסכת נזיר and מסכת סוטה that explains their order

steps.title: The order follows רבי's teaching about the סוטה and wine
steps.stepSummary: סוטה comes after נזיר because of רבי's lesson: anyone who sees a סוטה in her disgrace should stay away from wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי. A ברייתא teaches that רבי said: Why is the section of the נזיר placed next to the section of the סוטה in the תורה? To teach that anyone who sees a סוטה in her disgrace should keep himself away from wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 4. It says the connection between נזיר and סוטה comes from רבי's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the תורה, the section of נזיר comes right after the section of סוטה. רבי explains that seeing where wild behavior can lead should make a person stay away from wine. The משנה, which רבי arranged, follows the same link.

keyTerms.meaning: Was placed next to
Her ruin or disgrace
Should separate himself, as a נזיר does

phrases.english: It is in line with Rabbi.
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name is רבי יהודה הנשיא, the one who arranged the משנה.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi says:
Why was the section of the nazir placed next
to the section of the sotah?
phrases.notes: In the תורה: במדבר 5 is about the סוטה, and במדבר 6 is about the נזיר.

phrases.english: To tell you:
that anyone who sees a sotah in her disgrace
should keep himself away from wine.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מסכת סוטה is placed next to מסכת נזיר because of the link רבי draws between the two sections: anyone who sees a סוטה in her disgrace should keep away from wine.

steps.title: Then why not put סוטה first?
steps.stepSummary: If the order follows the תורה, סוטה should come before נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let him teach סוטה first, and afterward teach נזיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. In the תורה, סוטה comes first, so the tractates should be in that order too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's lesson works from סוטה to נזיר: you see the סוטה, and then you stay away from wine. So the answer from Step 5 seems to point to the opposite order from the one we have.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him teach
And afterward

phrases.english: But let him teach Sotah first,
and afterward teach Nazir!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the order of the tractates follows רבי's teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the תורה, סוטה comes first, so following רבי should put מסכת סוטה before מסכת נזיר.

steps.title: A chain of topics brought in נזיר first
steps.stepSummary: כתובות led to נדרים, נדרים led to נזיר, and only then did סוטה come, following רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he taught כתובות, which includes the chapter 'המדיר', he went on to teach נדרים. Since he taught נדרים, he taught נזיר, which is similar to vows. Then he teaches סוטה, following רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why נזיר ended up before סוטה. Each tractate led naturally into the next one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מסכת כתובות has a chapter about husbands who make vows, so the משנה continued with נדרים. נזיר is also a kind of vow, so it came next. After נזיר, רבי's link brought in סוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because it was already taught
One who makes a vow; the name of a chapter in כתובות
Is similar

steps.whatToRemember: The tractate order runs כתובות, then נדרים, then נזיר, then סוטה. Each one is linked to the tractate before it.

phrases.english: Since he taught Ketubot
and taught "One who vows,"
phrases.notes: This is the name of a chapter in כתובות about a husband who makes a vow against his wife.

phrases.english: he taught Nedarim.
And since he taught Nedarim
he taught Nazir, which is similar to vows.
And then he teaches Sotah, in line with Rabbi.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the order through a chain of related topics
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סוטה should have come first, as it does in the תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: נזיר came first because it follows נדרים. סוטה then comes right after נזיר, following רבי.

steps.title: 'One who warns' means a husband should not warn at the outset
steps.stepSummary: The wording 'המקנא' shows that our תנא holds it is forbidden to give a קינוי warning in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'one who warns.' That means after the fact, yes, the warning counts, but at the outset, no, he should not do it. Our תנא holds that it is forbidden to warn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the words of the משנה. It reads the opening word 'המקנא' closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not tell the husband to warn. It only describes a husband who already did. From this the גמרא learns that the warning works if it was given, but our תנא holds a husband should not give it to begin with.

keyTerms.meaning: One who warns his wife (קינוי)
After the fact
At the outset, in the first place
He holds
The תנא of our משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the warning has no effect. If a husband did warn, the warning counts. The rule is only that he should not warn in the first place.

phrases.english: "One who warns":
after the fact, yes;
at the outset, no.
Our Tanna holds:
it is forbidden to warn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the words of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to our תנא, a husband should not give a קינוי warning at the outset, but if he did give one, it counts.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a man's wife matches his deeds
steps.stepSummary: When ריש לקיש began teaching סוטה, he would say that a man is given a wife according to his deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said: When ריש לקיש began teaching סוטה, he would say this: A man is matched with a wife only according to his deeds, as it says, 'For the rod of wickedness shall not rest upon the lot of the righteous.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opening words ריש לקיש would say before teaching סוטה. He says a man's wife reflects how he acts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that wickedness does not land in the share of righteous people. So if a man ends up with a wife who acts like a סוטה, it reflects on his own deeds.

keyTerms.meaning: Opened, began teaching
Match a couple together
His deeds
Lot, portion

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה פָּתַח רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ בְּסוֹטָה,
phrases.english: When Reish Lakish would begin teaching Sotah,
he would say this:
A man is not matched with a wife
except according to his deeds,
as it says: "For the rod of wickedness shall not rest
upon the lot of the righteous."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה פָּתַח רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ בְּסוֹטָה, אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אגדה introduction to the topic of סוטה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man is matched with a wife according to his deeds.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: matching a couple is as hard as splitting the sea
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that matching a couple is as hard as קריעת ים סוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: And it is as hard to match them as the splitting of the Red Sea, as it says, 'God settles the lonely in a home; He brings out prisoners into prosperity.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds to the topic of matching couples. He says bringing a couple together is as hard as a huge miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places 'settling the lonely in a home' next to 'bringing out prisoners,' which refers to יציאת מצרים. This links matching a couple with the miracles of the Exodus, including קריעת ים סוף.

keyTerms.meaning: Are hard
The splitting of the Red Sea
Lonely, single people
Into prosperity, into a fitting state

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש teaches that a man's match depends on his deeds. רבי יוחנן teaches that making a match is as hard as קריעת ים סוף.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbah bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
And it is as hard to match them as the splitting of the Red Sea,
as it says: "God settles the lonely in a home,
He brings out prisoners into prosperity."
phrases.notes: "Bringing out prisoners" refers to יציאת מצרים, which is how the match gets compared to the sea splitting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְקָשִׁין לְזַוְּוגָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further teaching on the topic of matching couples from Step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Matching a couple is as hard as קריעת ים סוף.

steps.title: Aren't matches decreed before birth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a wife is given according to a man's deeds, quoting רב that a בת קול announces matches before a baby is even formed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רב יהודה said in the name of רב: forty days before a baby is formed, a heavenly voice goes out and says: the daughter of so-and-so will marry so-and-so, the house of so-and-so will belong to so-and-so, the field of so-and-so will belong to so-and-so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the earlier statement that a man gets a wife based on his deeds. It shows a teaching saying matches are fixed before birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If heaven announces the match before the child exists, the child has done no deeds yet. So the match cannot depend on his behavior. The two teachings seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening word that brings a challenge
The forming of the baby in the womb
A heavenly voice
So-and-so, a stand-in for any name

phrases.aramaic: אִינִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Is that so? But Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
phrases.notes: "Is that so" points back to the line that a man gets a wife according to his deeds.

phrases.english: Forty days before the forming of the baby
a heavenly voice goes out and says:
The daughter of so-and-so is for so-and-so,
the house of so-and-so is for so-and-so,
the field of so-and-so is for so-and-so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statements in steps 9–10 that matches depend on deeds and are hard to make.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a man is given a wife according to his deeds.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A match announced before birth cannot depend on deeds the person has not yet done.

steps.title: First match versus second match
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב's teaching is about a first marriage, and the deeds teaching is about a second marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about a first match, and that one is about a second match.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each teaching is talking about a different marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A first זיווג is set from heaven before birth. A second זיווג, such as after a divorce or a death, depends on a person's deeds. Each teaching now covers its own case, so they no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. A formula that opens an answer
A match or pairing of a couple
This one... that one. Assigns each source to its own case

steps.whatToRemember: A first match comes from heaven. A second match depends on a person's deeds.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one is about a first match,
phrases.notes: "This one" is רב's teaching about the heavenly voice.

phrases.english: that one is about a second match.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּזוּג רִאשׁוֹן, הָא בְּזוּג שֵׁנִי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different marriage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both teachings seemed to describe every marriage, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: A first marriage is decreed in heaven, and a second marriage depends on deeds.

steps.title: The argument is only about warning and seclusion
steps.stepSummary: Back to the משנה: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue only about the witnesses needed for קינוי and סתירה. For טומאה, one witness is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: he warns her based on two witnesses, and so on. They only argue about the warning and the seclusion. But about defilement, one witness is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's argument and makes a clear point about how far that argument goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about how many witnesses are needed for the warning (קינוי) and for the seclusion (סתירה). The גמרא notes that they do not argue about actual טומאה. There, both agree that a single witness is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: He warns her not to be alone with a certain man
They only argue up to this point. Limits the size of an argument
Seclusion: she was alone with that man after the warning
Here, actual adultery that forbids her to her husband
Is believed, is trusted

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the three stages: קינוי is the warning, סתירה is being alone, and טומאה is the actual sin. The argument is about the first two. One witness is enough for the third.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: מְקַנֵּא לָהּ עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: He warns her based on two witnesses, and so on.
They only argue
about the warning and the seclusion,
but about defilement, one witness is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא בְּקִינּוּי וּסְתִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and goes back to analyzing the משנה's argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides agree that one witness is believed about טומאה. They argue only about קינוי and סתירה.

steps.title: Another משנה backs this up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another משנה: if one witness says he saw her become טמאה, she does not drink the bitter water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we also learned: if one witness says, 'I saw that she was defiled,' she would not drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its point that one witness is believed about טומאה by quoting another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one witness were not believed, the woman would still drink to clear up the doubt. The משנה says she does not drink. That shows a single witness's testimony is accepted as fact.

keyTerms.meaning: And we also learned in a משנה. Brings a supporting source
Drinks the bitter water of the סוטה

phrases.english: And we also learned in a mishna:
If one witness says, "I saw that she was defiled" —
she would not drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule in step 13 with an outside משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That one witness is believed about טומאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A later משנה in this מסכת: one witness who saw her defiled stops her from drinking.

steps.title: Where does the תורה say one witness is believed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source in the תורה that one witness is believed about a סוטה's טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the תורה, how do we know that one witness is believed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source in the תורה for the rule it just showed from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the תורה needs two witnesses, so a single witness being believed is unusual. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this exception.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah itself
From where do we know? A request for a source

phrases.english: From the Torah, from where do we know
that one witness is believed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה's proof to asking for the Torah source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches one witness is believed about a סוטה's טומאה.

steps.title: The פסוק ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ means two witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer with a ברייתא: the פסוק ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ is talking about two witnesses. Steps 17 and 18 continue the ברייתא's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'And there is no witness against her' — the פסוק is speaking about two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering with a ברייתא about the פסוק. The full explanation comes next, so this step is setting it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word עד in the פסוק as meaning two witnesses, a full set. So the פסוק says she becomes forbidden when there are not two witnesses, only one. That means one witness is enough to forbid her. The ברייתא will explain this reading next.

keyTerms.meaning: And there is no witness against her (במדבר 5:13)
The פסוק is speaking about

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"And there is no witness against her":
the verse is speaking about two witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״, read as referring to a lack of two witnesses. This implies one witness is enough. The full explanation continues.

steps.title: Maybe the word עד means even one witness
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: maybe ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ is not about two witnesses, but means there was not even one witness?
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the פסוק means that there was not even one witness?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own claim that ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ is about two witnesses. It suggests the word עד might mean even a single witness, and this sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עד is singular, so a simple reading would be 'not even one witness.' If that were right, the פסוק would only cover a case where no witness at all saw the טומאה. The ברייתא raises this reading so that it can reject it with a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only... (a formula that offers another possible reading)
even with one (witness)
a witness (singular form), here the question is whether it means one or two

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that because עד is a singular word it must mean one witness. The whole point of the ברייתא is to show that in the תורה a plain עד usually means two witnesses.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it means even [not] one?
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added to help the meaning: maybe ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ means not even one witness saw her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in Step 16, that ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ refers to two witnesses.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the singular word עד in ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ refer to two witnesses or to even one witness?

steps.title: Proof from the פסוק about one witness
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes ״לֹא יָקוּם עֵד אֶחָד בְּאִישׁ״. The תורה had to add the word אחד, so a plain עד means two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'One witness shall not rise up against a man.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question by quoting a פסוק from דברים. This פסוק shows that the word עד on its own means two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ״לֹא יָקוּם עֵד אֶחָד״ the תורה adds the word אחד when it wants to say 'one witness.' That means a plain עד, with no number attached, refers to two witnesses. So the earlier reading stands, and ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ means there were not two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק teaches / comes to say (introduces a proof from a פסוק)
shall not rise up (shall not be enough to establish a matter)
one witness, with the extra word אחד making it clearly singular

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that a plain עד in the תורה means two, is the base for the coming proof that one witness is believed about a סוטה's טומאה.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"One witness shall not rise up against a man."
phrases.notes: דברים 19:15. Notice the תורה has to add the word 'one' when it means a single witness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17 by quoting a פסוק that shows a plain עד means two witnesses.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since the תורה writes ״עֵד אֶחָד״ when it means a single witness, a plain עד refers to two witnesses. So ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״ means there were not two witnesses.
